This technical reference accompanies the [Oxfordshire–Uxbridge Decision Brief](uptake_case_study.qmd). It brings together the empirical trip-purpose evidence, full Propensity to Cycle Tool (PCT) and temporal ramp-up equations, DfT **Active Mode Appraisal Toolkit (AMAT)** valuation formulas and benchmark validation, the audit of existing `railactive` prototype scripts, supplementary corridor diagnostics, and the standardised 4-table hand-off schema aligned with Active Travel England's *Active Mode Benefits: Theoretical Framework* [@nellthorp2026].

## Travel Demand & Empirical Trip Purpose Evidence {#sec-purpose}

Traditional transport appraisal tools frequently focus solely on the commute-to-work (e.g. Census Journey to Work matrices or the PCT commute layer). For a regional or national spine route like the HS2 greenway, this introduces severe undercounting risk. Analysis of recent UK microdata shows how active travel distributes across purposes:

- **National Travel Survey (NTS, 2022–2024):**
  - **Leisure cycling ({{< var nts_cycle_leisure_pct >}})** is the single largest cycling purpose, outstripping commuting ({{< var nts_cycle_commute_pct >}}).
  - **Leisure walking ({{< var nts_walk_leisure_pct >}})** dominates walking trips (42.5% "just walk"), whereas commuting accounts for only {{< var nts_walk_commute_pct >}}.
  - **Trip length & duration:** Leisure cycle trips average **4.20 miles ({{< var nts_cycle_leisure_km >}}) and 29.9 minutes**, versus **3.43 miles ({{< var nts_cycle_commute_km >}}) and 22.9 minutes** for commuting (31% longer per trip).
- **Sport England Active Lives Survey (ALS, Year 9, 2023–2024):**
  - **Participation:** 31.9% of adults cycle for leisure/sport annually versus 11.3% for travel.
  - **Activity volume:** Leisure represents **{{< var als_cycle_leisure_time_pct >}} of total cycling minutes** and **61.5% of total walking minutes**.

| Metric | Leisure / Exercise | Commute / Travel |
| :--- | :---: | :---: |
| Cycling Trips (NTS) | {{< var nts_cycle_leisure_pct >}} | {{< var nts_cycle_commute_pct >}} |
| Cycling Time (ALS) | {{< var als_cycle_leisure_time_pct >}} | {{< var als_cycle_travel_time_pct >}} |
| Walking Trips (NTS) | {{< var nts_walk_leisure_pct >}} | {{< var nts_walk_commute_pct >}} |

## PCT Logistic Propensity Specification {#sec-pct-details}

Under Random Utility Maximisation (RUM), commute cycling share $p_{ij}$ on $(i, j)$ follows a logistic function of utility difference $\Delta V_{ij} = -\lambda\,(GC^{\text{cycle}}_{ij} - GC^{\text{alt}}_{ij})$:

$$
\text{logit}\bigl(p_{ij}\bigr) = \ln\!\left(\frac{p_{ij}}{1 - p_{ij}}\right) = \alpha(q_{ij}) + f(d_{ij},\, g_{ij})
$$ {#eq-logit}

In the UK Propensity to Cycle Tool [@lovelace2017], calibrated on 2011 Census OD flows across England and Wales, the baseline distance–hilliness decay function for fastest-route distance $d_{ij}$ (km) and average gradient $g_{ij}$ (%) is:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{logit}\bigl(p^{\text{base}}_{ij}\bigr) &= -3.818 - 0.652\,d_{ij} + 2.084\sqrt{d_{ij}} + 0.00878\,d_{ij}^2 \\
&\quad - 0.256\,g_{ij} + 0.0199\,d_{ij}g_{ij} - 0.123\sqrt{d_{ij}}\,g_{ij}
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-pct-base}

Area-wide transformation to *Go Dutch* shifts the infrastructure-quality intercept ($\Delta \alpha_{\text{Dutch}} = +2.552$, with slope term $-0.079\,d_{ij}$), while *E-bikes* additionally attenuates distance and gradient exertion penalties $e(t)$ [@nellthorp2026, §4.2.3].

## Temporal Adoption & Health-Lag Equations {#sec-temporal-equations}

Cumulative behavioural adoption $r(t) \in [0, 1]$ at $t$ years post-opening follows a **Bass diffusion S-curve** [@bass1969] with innovation parameter $p$ and imitation parameter $q$:

$$
r(t) = \frac{1 - e^{-(p + q)t}}{1 + \frac{q}{p}\,e^{-(p + q)t}}
$$ {#eq-bass}

In appraisal year $y \ge oy$ (mid-year $t_y = y - oy + 0.5$), daily trips equal:

$$
\Delta T_y = \Delta T^{*} \cdot r(t_y) \cdot (1 + g_{\text{bg}})^{\min(y - oy,\, 20)}
$$ {#eq-annual-trips}

where $\Delta T^{*}$ is steady-state uptake and $g_{\text{bg}} = 0.0075$ is AMAT's annual background growth rate. Convolving annual conversion cohorts $\Delta r_j = r(t_j) - r(t_{j-1})$ with AMAT's 5-year linear physiological mortality lag gives the effective health-benefit share $H^{\text{eff}}_k$ in operational year $k$:

$$
H^{\text{eff}}_k = \sum_{j=1}^{k} \Delta r_j \cdot \min\!\bigl(1,\; 0.2\,(k - j + 1)\bigr)
$$ {#eq-conv}

Sensitivity profiles evaluated in the Decision Brief use $(p=0.22, q=0.70)$ for Fast (3-yr), $(p=0.10, q=0.55)$ for Central (5-yr), and $(p=0.05, q=0.35)$ for Slow (8-yr) maturity.

## Economic Benefits Appraisal (DfT AMAT) & Validation {#sec-amat}

Economic benefits are evaluated using a verified base-R implementation of DfT AMAT ([`railactive/amat`](https://github.com/railactive/amat)) across four main benefit streams:

1. **Premature Death Reduction (Health):** Uses the WHO HEAT dose-response curve adapted for TAG, valued using discounted Years of Life Lost (YLL) at £92,240 per life-year across 5 age bands by sex:

   $$\text{RR} = \max\!\left(0.55,\; \exp\!\left(\frac{\ln(0.90)}{11.25} \times \text{MET-hours/week}\right)\right)$$

2. **Workplace Absenteeism:** Sickness absence reduction (0.25 days/user/year) applied to employed new users, valued at average regional daily labour output (£267.36/day).
3. **Journey Ambience & Quality:** Valued using the **Rule of a Half** for existing and new trips (upgrading from "No provision" to "Off-road segregated cycle track" yields **{{< var ambience_offroad_rate >}}**):

   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   \text{Benefit} &= \left(\text{Trips}_{\text{existing}} + \frac{\text{Trips}_{\text{new}}}{2}\right) \\
                  &\quad \times \Delta\text{Rate} \times \text{Time on Scheme} \times \text{VoT}_{\text{non-work}}
   \end{aligned}
   $$

4. **Decongestion & Environmental Externalities:** Mode shift from cars and taxis reduces vehicle-kilometres across 7 marginal external cost streams (congestion, infrastructure, collisions, local air quality, noise, GHGs, and indirect tax):

   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   \text{Vehicle-km Reduced} &= \text{Trips}_{\text{new}} \times \text{Trip Length} \times \text{Days} \\
                             &\quad \times \left(\frac{\text{Car Divert}}{\text{Car Occupancy}} + \frac{\text{Taxi Divert}}{\text{Taxi Occupancy}}\right)
   \end{aligned}
   $$

## Audit of Existing RailActive Prototype Work {#sec-audit}

Before specifying the appraisal-ready pipeline, we audited analytical outputs across `railactive/pipeline`, `railactive/hs2cycle`, and `railactive/amat`:

- **Harmonised corridor alignment (`north_south_corridor_v2.json`, {{< var corridor_version >}}):** {{< var corridor_total_km >}} km preferred North–South Greenway spine ({{< var corridor_hs2_km >}} km core HS2 alignment plus Avenue Verte and Stoke–Birkenhead branches) with a 3-tier status taxonomy (`preferred`, `alternative`, `superseded`) and civil-asset classes (`Repurposed HS2 TCR`, `HS2 delivered greenway`, `Dual Use MATs`).
- **Multi-purpose network assignment (`pipeline` Phases 1–4):** Splicing the preferred greenway into a 1.72M-link corridor network in Rust/CSIS `netassign` (DEM gradients capped at $\pm 2\%$ on engineered alignments) and validating against **7,219 cycling** and **1,439 walking** counters lifted baseline cycling fit from $R^2_{\log 10} = 0.352$ (commute-only) to **$0.676$** (`56.2%` within $2\times$), and walking fit from $-0.177$ to **$0.488$**. Phase 2 separated route diversion (`+3,175` bike pkm/day) from induced/shifted commute demand (`+4,953` bike pkm/day); Phase 4 lifted spine cycling from `86.7` to `132.3` riders/day (`+52.6%`).

Five structural prototype gaps must be resolved before full-corridor business-case modelling:

```{r tbl-audit-gaps}
#| tbl-colwidths: [5, 33, 30, 32]

  "data/uptake_audit_gaps.csv",

  align = c("r", "l", "l", "l"),
  col_names = c("#", "Current Prototype Implementation", "Economic / Appraisal Risk", "Required Upgrade")
)
```

## Standardised Demand-to-AMAT Output Contract {#sec-outputs}

To bridge spatial demand outputs cleanly into [`railactive/amat`](https://github.com/railactive/amat), TAG worksheets, and ATE's forthcoming **TATE3030** tool without manual spreadsheet post-processing, the pipeline exports four standardised tables:

```{r tbl-outputs}
#| tbl-colwidths: [20, 20, 35, 25]
tbl_from_csv(
  "data/uptake_outputs_schema.csv",
  caption = "Standardised four-table output contract between the RailActive demand pipeline and economic evaluation tools.",
  align = c("l", "l", "l", "l"),
  col_names = c("Output Dataset", "Granularity", "Key Fields & Units", "Economic Appraisal Consumer")
)
```
